Fathomable

/FATH-um-uh-bul/ — stress on FATH · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something fathomable can be understood or figured out, even if it takes real effort.

After the third diagram, the engine's design finally became fathomable.

Worked Example

The ancient manuscript's meaning finally became fathomable after the historian found a matching text in the archives.

Fathom means to measure water depth, and figuratively, to understand or 'get to the bottom of' something. Fathom + -able (able to be done) = able to be gotten to the bottom of. Since fathom is a whole English word, it takes -able. The scenario shows understanding required effort and patience, but eventual comprehension was achievable—exactly what fathomable promises.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

understandable: able to be grasped without great difficulty

comprehensible: able to be fully grasped mentally

decipherable: able to be decoded with careful effort

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

unfathomable: too deep to ever be understood

baffling: so confusing it cannot be figured out

Where it sits · how fully it can be understood — intelligible → decipherable → explicable → fathomable

intelligible vs. fathomable: An intelligible announcement can at least be made out, while a fathomable idea can be understood all the way down.

decipherable vs. fathomable: A decipherable code can be cracked piece by piece, but a fathomable mystery can be fully understood once you work through it.

explicable vs. fathomable: An explicable event can be explained in a sentence or two; a fathomable one can be truly gotten to the bottom of, however deep it runs.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — fathom

Root — fathom: originally 'outstretched arms,' then a six-foot measure of water depth, then 'to measure the depth of — to get to the bottom of' (Old English (faethm))

Suffix — -able

Suffix — -able: able to be; capable of being (Latin (-abilis))

Put it together

Put it together: fathom ('to get to the bottom of,' the way sailors once measured water depth with outstretched arms of rope) + -able = able to be gotten to the bottom of — understandable, even when it is deep or complicated and takes real effort.

Use the root in a new word: fathomless

Use the root in a new word: fathomless: Scientists lowered their instruments into the fathomless darkness of the ocean trench.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral-to-formal

Use fathomable when something is genuinely difficult to understand but not impossible—like a complex theory, a contradictory person's motives, or a challenging text. It's more precise than 'understandable' because it emphasizes the depth of effort required and promises eventual comprehension.
